papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.abstract: We introduce BERT, a new method of pre-training general-purpose language representations using bidirectional transformers. Unlike previous work, we show that bidirectional pre-training of transformers allows for a more powerful understanding of language context.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the NISQ era and beyond
papers.abstract: Quantum computers will be useful in the near future for various applications despite the presence of significant noise in their operations. We describe algorithms for near-term quantum computers and discuss the challenges of implementing them.

papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated substantial gains on many NLP tasks by pre-training on a diverse corpus of text followed by fine-tuning on a specific task. Here we show that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance.

papers.title: Supervised learning with quantum enhanced feature spaces
papers.abstract: We propose and experimentally implement novel methods on a superconducting processor that represent the feature space of a classification problem by a quantum state, taking advantage of the large dimensionality of quantum Hilbert space to obtain an enhanced solution.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We achieve state-of-the-art results on ImageNet and other benchmarks.

papers.title: Extending the computational reach of a noisy superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Quantum computation benefits from theoretically proven speed-ups for certain problems. Recent theoretical work has shown that the accuracy of computation based on expectation values of quantum observables can be enhanced through error mitigation. Here we demonstrate this protocol on a superconducting quantum processor.

papers.title: "Why Should I Trust You?": Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce LIME, a model-agnostic technique for interpreting the predictions of any classifier. The technique allows users to understand why the classification was made by learning simple and interpretable models locally around the prediction.
